source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Tracing the USB nets in KiCad points to what I think is the cause: the USBLC6-2SC6 ESD component U3 has its VBUS pin 5 connected to GND rather than +5V. The D+/D- routing itself appears correct, running from connector pins A6/B6/A7/B7 through U3 to GPIO20 (D+) and GPIO19 (D-).

execution.observed_behavior: After native USB failed on all three integrated-board samples, KiCad net tracing showed that USBLC6-2SC6 U3 pin 5 was connected to GND instead of +5V.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: To restore ESD protection properly, please correct the symbol: connect pin 5 (VBUS) to +5V, route pin 2 separately to GND instead of tying the two together, and retain the D+/D- pass-through via U3. When USBLC6 is wired correctly, protection returns and USB operates. Is that what you intend to change? There is no rush; I will continue testing meanwhile.

value_updates.ground_pin_2_connection: GND on a separate net from VBUS

routing_warnings.description: The failure to enumerate in normal and forced-download modes is direct runtime evidence for native USB operation; it is only supporting context for the ESD-protection wiring failure.
Successful USB operation after removing U3 and bridging the data lines verifies the native USB path, not ESD protection, because the workaround leaves ESD protection absent.
